PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), and no hardware was attached or run.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], xmls/lab_env.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. The scene root is '<mujoco model="ur5">' (xmls/lab_env.xml:1); it has 14 one-DOF joints (six arm hinges plus eight finger hinges) and four target bodies of three slide joints and one ball joint each, so the bridge state has 42 qpos and 38 qvel values, and 12 active motor actuators (xmls/lab_env.xml:232-243; the velocity and position blocks are XML comments). cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [12 numbers]}}; the bridge writes data.ctrl, runs mj_step for ticks and returns the observation {time, qpos, qvel}, tick and state_hash. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The model's <option timestep="0.02"> (xmls/lab_env.xml:4) gives a 20 ms lockstep step. The active motors declare neither ctrlrange nor ctrllimited, so MuJoCo's default leaves them unlimited and the bridge derives no control interval; the package declares no Limit and no operator-required bound because the model file is the system of record for the control envelope and states none. The action is therefore unbounded in this simulated R0 package.

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card's family-config decision and MujocoDriver helper express the served MJCF scene, so there is no deviation from the card. The upstream environment.py is a task environment around the model (initial_pos and joint_pos reset at :89-92, a four-element action mapping at :103-111, two cropped 214x214 camera images plus grasp/danger at :170-188) and needs mujoco-py 1.5 plus gym, cv2 and scipy (README.md:5-6, environment.py:2-14). MuJoCo and mujoco-py are not installed and cannot be installed here (no network, no pip), and package code never imports the clone. backends['fake'] is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library (fake.py), named .fake:FakeMujoco in the lock; it parses the same XML for the joint dimensions, actuator count, control targets and absent ctrlrange, but its integration is a placeholder first-order motion and it resolves no contact, equality, tendon, mesh, texture, sensor or camera. A backend name not listed (sim) would import the real mujoco module; that path was not run. The clone was not modified or imported, and the card lists no entry_symbols, so there was no symbol to verify.

NOT COVERED: the upstream task interface is not served, so its reset state, four-element action mapping, two cropped 214x214 camera images (from 960x720 renders) and grasp/danger outputs are NOT COVERED. MuJoCo itself was never imported, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine; the fake is not MuJoCo physics. No physical UR5 or Robotiq gripper is modelled or driven, and nothing was validated against hardware. The clone has no LICENSE file, so [...]
